name: chrome
title: Google Chrome
what: The Chrome web browser. Each tab and extension runs as its own process, so you'll see many of these.
notes: Memory use grows with open tabs. Chrome's Memory Saver (Settings > Performance) puts unused tabs to sleep.

name: msedge
title: Microsoft Edge
what: The Edge web browser. Each tab and extension runs as its own process.
notes: Edge's Efficiency mode and Sleeping tabs (Settings > System and performance) reduce memory use.

name: firefox
title: Mozilla Firefox
what: The Firefox web browser.
notes: Many open tabs and add-ons increase memory use.

name: msedgewebview2
title: Microsoft Edge WebView2
what: A shared browser component that many apps (Teams, Outlook, widgets) use to show their windows.
notes: High usage usually comes from whichever app is using it, not WebView2 itself.

name: onedrive
title: Microsoft OneDrive
what: Syncs your files to the cloud.
notes: Can use a lot of disk and network while syncing large folders. You can pause syncing from its tray icon.

name: googledrivefs
title: Google Drive
what: Syncs your files with Google Drive.
notes: Heavy disk use during large syncs.

name: dropbox
title: Dropbox
what: Syncs your files with Dropbox.
notes: Heavy disk use during large syncs; can be paused from its tray icon.

name: ms-teams
title: Microsoft Teams
what: Chat and video meetings app.
notes: Uses a lot of memory and CPU during video calls.

name: teams
title: Microsoft Teams (classic)
what: The older version of Teams.
notes: Known for high memory use; the new Teams is lighter.

name: discord
title: Discord
what: Voice, video and text chat app popular with gamers.
notes: Hardware acceleration and overlays can affect games.

name: slack
title: Slack
what: Work chat app.
notes: Memory grows with the number of workspaces.

name: zoom
title: Zoom
what: Video meetings app.
notes: Heavy CPU use during calls with video effects.

name: spotify
title: Spotify
what: Music streaming app.
notes: Caches music on disk; usually light.

name: steam
title: Steam
what: Game store and launcher.
notes: Downloads and game updates can use a lot of disk and network.

name: steamwebhelper
title: Steam web helper
what: Draws Steam's store and library windows.
notes: Can use noticeable CPU/GPU while the Steam window is open.

name: epicgameslauncher
title: Epic Games Launcher
what: Game store and launcher.
notes: Known to use CPU even when idle; close it while gaming if not needed.

name: battle.net
title: Battle.net
what: Game launcher for Blizzard games.

name: riotclientservices
title: Riot Client
what: Launcher for Riot games.
notes: Don't touch vgc (Vanguard anti-cheat).

name: vgc
title: Riot Vanguard
what: Anti-cheat for Riot games.
notes: Changing anti-cheat processes can get your game account flagged.

name: easyanticheat
title: Easy Anti-Cheat
what: Anti-cheat used by many games.
notes: Never change anti-cheat processes.

name: obs64
title: OBS Studio
what: Screen recording and streaming app.
notes: Throttling it while recording causes dropped frames.

name: code
title: Visual Studio Code
what: Code editor.
notes: Extensions can use a lot of CPU and memory.

name: devenv
title: Visual Studio
what: Programming environment.
notes: Heavy memory use with large projects.

name: outlook
title: Microsoft Outlook (classic)
what: Email and calendar app.
notes: Large mailboxes and add-ins slow it down.

name: olk
title: Microsoft Outlook (new)
what: The new Outlook email app.

name: winword
title: Microsoft Word
what: Word processor.

name: excel
title: Microsoft Excel
what: Spreadsheet app.
notes: Large spreadsheets with many formulas can use a lot of CPU.

name: acrobat
title: Adobe Acrobat
what: PDF viewer and editor.

name: creative cloud
title: Adobe Creative Cloud
what: Manages Adobe apps and syncs files.
notes: Runs several background helpers (CCXProcess, AdobeIPCBroker) even when no Adobe app is open.

name: ccxprocess
title: Adobe Creative Cloud helper
what: Background helper for Adobe Creative Cloud.
notes: Safe to stop from starting automatically if you rarely use Adobe apps.

name: searchindexer
title: Windows Search Indexer
what: Builds the index that makes Start menu and File Explorer search fast.
notes: Busy after big file changes or updates; settles down on its own.

name: searchhost
title: Windows Search
what: The search box in the Start menu and taskbar.

name: msmpeng
title: Microsoft Defender Antivirus
what: Windows' built-in antivirus. It scans files to keep you safe.
notes: Scans can use lots of CPU and disk for a while; they usually run when the PC is idle. Never disable or throttle it.

name: mpdefendercoreservice
title: Microsoft Defender core service
what: Part of Windows' built-in antivirus.
notes: Protected security component.

name: tiworker
title: Windows Modules Installer Worker
what: Installs Windows updates.
notes: Heavy CPU and disk use during updates is normal and temporary. Let it finish.

name: trustedinstaller
title: Windows Modules Installer
what: Installs and repairs Windows components and updates.
notes: Temporary; let it finish.

name: mousocoreworker
title: Windows Update helper
what: Checks for and orchestrates Windows updates.

name: compattelrunner
title: Microsoft Compatibility Telemetry
what: Collects compatibility and diagnostic data for Windows.
notes: Can cause short bursts of disk and CPU use, usually when idle.

name: vmmem
title: Virtual machine memory (WSL / Hyper-V)
what: Memory and CPU used by virtual machines, including WSL and Docker.
notes: Its usage is whatever is running inside the virtual machine. Shutting down WSL (wsl --shutdown) frees it.

name: vmmemwsl
title: WSL memory
what: Memory used by the Windows Subsystem for Linux.
notes: You can cap it in .wslconfig, or free it with wsl --shutdown.

name: com.docker.backend
title: Docker Desktop
what: Runs Docker containers.
notes: Uses memory through vmmem while running.

name: dwm
title: Desktop Window Manager
what: Draws everything on your screen.
notes: Essential Windows process. High usage usually comes from many open windows, animations or a graphics driver issue.

name: explorer
title: Windows Explorer
what: The taskbar, Start menu and File Explorer.
notes: Essential. If it's stuck, restarting it from Task Manager fixes most issues.

name: svchost
title: Service Host
what: Runs Windows background services. There are always many of these.
notes: Essential. If one is busy, the cause is the service inside it (often Windows Update or SysMain).

name: runtimebroker
title: Runtime Broker
what: Manages permissions for Store apps.
notes: Usually light; high usage points to a misbehaving Store app.

name: backgroundtaskhost
title: Background Task Host
what: Runs short background tasks for apps.

name: wmiprvse
title: WMI Provider Host
what: Answers system-information requests from other programs.
notes: High CPU means another program is asking it lots of questions; find that program instead.

name: audiodg
title: Windows Audio Device Graph
what: Processes all sound on your PC.
notes: Throttling it causes audio crackling.

name: csrss
title: Client Server Runtime
what: Core Windows process.
notes: Essential; never touch it.

name: lsass
title: Local Security Authority
what: Handles sign-in and security.
notes: Essential; never touch it.

name: memory compression
title: Memory Compression
what: Windows compresses memory to fit more in RAM instead of using the slow disk.
notes: High numbers here mean the PC is short on memory, not that this is a problem itself.

name: nvdisplay.container
title: NVIDIA Display Container
what: Part of the NVIDIA graphics driver (control panel and settings).
notes: Usually light.

name: nvcontainer
title: NVIDIA Container
what: Runs NVIDIA app features like overlays and recording.
notes: Overlay and Instant Replay features use extra resources.

name: radeonsoftware
title: AMD Radeon Software
what: AMD graphics driver settings and overlays.

name: phoneexperiencehost
title: Phone Link
what: Connects your phone to your PC.
notes: Can be turned off from starting automatically if unused.

name: widgets
title: Windows Widgets
what: The news and weather widgets panel.
notes: Can be turned off in taskbar settings.

name: smartscreen
title: Windows Defender SmartScreen
what: Checks downloads and apps for safety.
notes: Security component.
